findings.title: Stop hook is already async but has a 10s timeout that likely truncates Ollama work
findings.detail: session-learning-check.sh is registered with `async: true` and `timeout: 10` in settings.json. However, the hook calls signal_processor.py which embeds 10 prototype sentences (10 Ollama calls at ~100ms each = ~1s) plus up to MAX_EMBEDDING_CALLS_PER_SESSION=5 per-message calls, plus correction_groups embedding work. With the 10s timeout, sections 3-6 of the hook may get killed before completing. The tracking stop-hook.sh has a 30s timeout and runs 4+ Python scripts sequentially. Combined, these two async Stop hooks compete for Ollama resources.

findings.title: OpenMemory has 749 entries; 366 are transcript/correction bloat outside budget enforcement
findings.detail: OpenMemory contains 261 transcript entries (tags like 'transcript,session-2026-03-*') and 105 correction/behavioral entries that predate the budget system. The ALLOWED_TAGS whitelist in om_write.py does NOT include 'transcript' or 'correction' tags, meaning these were written before the gate existed. Budget enforcement (max 20 session-summary, 30 behavioral-pref, etc.) only applies to new writes — it never retroactively prunes legacy entries. 366 of 749 entries (49%) are legacy bloat. The 4.5MB DB stores 644 entries with embeddings and 105 without.

findings.title: correction-tallies.jsonl is legacy dead code with only 2 entries
findings.detail: correction-tallies.jsonl has 2 entries and is only consumed by _parse_corrections() in signal_processor.py to skip already-promoted entries. Since correction_groups DB table now tracks promotion status directly, this file is redundant. The only reader checks `entry.get('promoted')` — the same data is in `correction_groups.status='promoted'`.

findings.title: om-ops.json is 2781 lines of append-only ops log with no consumer
findings.detail: om-ops.json logs every write/dedup/prune/error operation from om_write.py. It has 2781 entries. No code reads this file — it is write-only diagnostic data. It grows unbounded. The useful signal (dedup rates, write failures) could be a SQLite table with aggregation, or simply removed if the budget/dedup system is working correctly.

findings.title: tool-learnings.md has 3 entries and is shadowed to OpenMemory (29 OM entries)
findings.detail: tool-learnings.md is an append-only audit trail with 3 entries. The Stop hook (Section 5) reads every non-AUTO entry and writes each to OpenMemory via om_write. OpenMemory has 29 tool-learning entries. The flat file is the 'source of truth' but contains far less than OM. The sync is one-directional (file -> OM) and re-runs every session, deduping via embedding similarity. This is O(n*m) embedding work on every session end for 3 entries.

findings.title: corrections.md is both human-editable source of truth AND machine-parsed input
findings.detail: corrections.md (30+ entries, ~170 lines) serves dual roles: (1) human-readable log that Claude and user both write to, (2) input to _parse_corrections() which embeds each entry and clusters into correction_groups. This dual role means the file can't be moved to SQLite without breaking the user's editing workflow. The shadow-table pattern (keep md, ingest to DB) is already partially implemented via process_session_corrections().

findings.title: Ollama dependency is load-bearing for correction detection but has graceful degradation
findings.detail: decision-74 chose semantic embeddings over regex for correction detection. When Ollama is down: (1) extract_corrections() returns empty list (no corrections detected), (2) om_write dedup falls back to simhash, (3) _process_correction_groups() skips entirely. The system silently loses all correction detection capability when Ollama is unavailable. The MAX_EMBEDDING_CALLS_PER_SESSION=5 cap already limits the embedding tax. At <500 entries, a character n-gram Jaccard approach could replace prototype matching without Ollama, but this conflicts with decision-74's explicit rejection of non-semantic approaches.

findings.title: Duplicate embedding infrastructure: signal_processor.py and om_write.py both implement _get_embedding, _cosine_similarity, blob serialization
findings.detail: Both files independently implement: _get_embedding() (Ollama HTTP call), _cosine_similarity() (dot product), _embedding_to_blob()/_blob_to_embedding() (struct pack/unpack), and _compute_simhash() (in om_write). This is ~80 lines of duplicated code. A shared embedding_utils.py module would eliminate this.

findings.title: rendered-prefs.md is currently empty (schema migration pending) — the entire preference rendering pipeline is dormant
findings.detail: rendered-prefs.md contains only '# Behavioral Preferences\n\n_Schema migration pending._' The SessionStart hook's Python block checks for a 'text' column in correction_groups and writes empty if missing. However, the correction_groups table DOES have a 'text' column (added in session-learning-check.sh Section 6b schema migration). The render query requires status IN ('promoted','pending_promotion') OR source='manual' — current data shows 4 promoted and 0 pending_promotion with source='manual'. The text field on those 4 promoted rows may be empty, causing the sidecar to appear blank despite promoted entries existing.

architecture_patterns.name: Tiered dedup (fast-reject + semantic)
architecture_patterns.description: Tier 1: exact MD5 hash match (microseconds). Tier 2: character trigram Jaccard >= 0.8 (sub-ms for <500 entries). Tier 3: embedding cosine similarity only for borderline cases (Jaccard 0.4-0.8). Reduces Ollama calls by ~90% at current scale.

architecture_patterns.name: Background detach with PID lockfile
architecture_patterns.description: Double-fork pattern: redirect all streams to /tmp log, write PID file, use SQLite WAL mode with busy_timeout=5000. Check PID file before starting to prevent duplicate runs. Though the Stop hook is already async, the 10s timeout likely kills long-running embedding work. Alternative: split the hook into fast (mtime check, DB reads) and slow (embedding work) sections, running slow section via nohup.
architecture_patterns.applicability: session-learning-check.sh — split sections 1-2 (fast, <1s) from sections 3-6 (slow, Ollama-dependent)

architecture_patterns.name: System-state vs user-knowledge split
architecture_patterns.description: Machine-consumed data (om-ops.json, correction-tallies.jsonl, tool-learnings sync) goes to SQLite tables. Human-editable data (corrections.md) stays as flat files with shadow-table ingestion. Currently 4 of 7 surfaces are machine-only and could consolidate.

architecture_patterns.name: One-time legacy purge for OpenMemory
architecture_patterns.description: Delete 261 transcript entries and 105 correction/behavioral entries that predate the budget system. These tags are not in ALLOWED_TAGS and will never be written again. Reduces DB from 749 to ~383 entries and reclaims ~2MB of embedding storage.

conflicts.conflict_description: decision-74 explicitly chose semantic embeddings over regex for correction detection and rejected fallback. Any proposal to replace Ollama-based correction detection with n-gram/Jaccard/keyword approaches for the prototype matching step directly conflicts. However: (1) the decision was about regex specifically, not about all non-neural approaches, (2) dedup in om_write.py already has a simhash fallback that decision-74 didn't address, (3) the 'no regex fallback' stance means corrections are silently lost when Ollama is down.
resolution_options: Keep decision-74 for correction detection, only remove Ollama from dedup (where simhash fallback already exists)
Supersede decision-74 with evidence that character n-gram Jaccard captures semantic similarity better than regex while still being non-neural
Implement tiered approach: simhash for dedup, keep Ollama only for correction prototype matching (reduces Ollama calls from ~15 to ~5 per session)

conflicts.conflict_description: corrections.md serves as both human-editable correction log and machine input for correction grouping. Moving it to SQLite breaks the human editing workflow. Keeping it means maintaining the parse-and-embed pipeline.
resolution_options: Shadow table pattern: keep corrections.md as source of truth, use mtime-based change detection to trigger DB re-sync only when modified
Accept the dual role, consolidate everything else into DB
